claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know that you have Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: Are you or Alex currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Next, I need to ask: Are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, do you have the main responsibility for caring for Alex on a day-to-day basis?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm responsible for Alex and take care of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask: Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more important question: Are you or your partner (if you have one) subject to immigration control, or do either of you have any restrictions on your right to reside in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're not subject to immigration control and don't have any restrictions on our right to reside in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information.

Just to confirm I have everything I need: Is there anything else about your circumstances or Alex's situation that might be relevant? For example:
- Does Alex live with you full-time, or is there a shared care arrangement with another parent?
- Is Alex in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex does live with me full-time. Actually, there is something I should mention - Alex has been in hospital for a few months now. I haven't really been able to afford to spend money on their needs while they're in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. I understand that must be a difficult situation for you and Alex.

The fact that Alex is in hospital is important for the assessment. I need to ask: Has Alex been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks, or is it expected that the stay will be less than 12 weeks in total?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been more than 12 weeks now - about 15 weeks actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for clarifying that Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks.

This is an important detail. I need to ask: During Alex's hospital stay, have you been contributing to the cost of Alex's upkeep? For example, have you been spending money on things like clothing, toys, books, or other items for Alex's needs while in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been able to. As I mentioned, I haven't been able to afford to spend money on their needs while they're in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I understand this has been financially difficult for you.

I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, based on the information you've provided, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. Here's why:

Under UK Child Benefit rules, if a child has been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if you are contributing to the cost of the child's upkeep during their hospital stay. Since Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks (which is more than 12 weeks) and you have not been able to contribute financially to Alex's upkeep during this time, you would not meet the eligibility criteria.

However, it's important to note that once Alex leaves hospital and returns home to live with you, you should be able to claim Child Benefit again, as you would resume full responsibility for their care and upkeep.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this decision or Child Benefit in general?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So just to be clear, once Alex comes home from the hospital, I can claim it then?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct. Once Alex comes home from the hospital and is living with you again, you should be able to claim Child Benefit, as you would meet the eligibility criteria at that point:

- Alex will be under 16 (currently 8 years old)
- Alex will be living with you
- You will be responsible for Alex's care and upkeep
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You're not subject to immigration control

You would need to make a new claim (or inform Child Benefit if you currently have an existing claim that has stopped) once Alex returns home.

Let me now formally record the eligibility assessment for your case.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I hope Alex recovers soon and can come home. If you have any other questions in the future, please don't hesitate to ask. Take care.
